name: jetson_orin_nano_core
description: One Vortex core given one GPU core's (SM's) share of the Jetson Orin Nano Super memory system: 1/8 of its 128-bit LPDDR5-6400 (102.4 GB/s) and 1/8 of its GPU L2, at the 1020 MHz GPU clock. Battlefield step, 27 Nov 2026.

sources.NUM_CORES: One core stands for one of the Orin Nano's 8 GPU cores (1024 CUDA cores, 32 tensor cores = 8 Ampere SMs)
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_*: 128-bit LPDDR5 at 6400 MT/s = 102.4 GB/s (NVIDIA: 102 GB/s for the Super kit), split 8 ways: one x16 channel of 2 B x 6.4 GT/s = 12.8 GB/s per core. Vortex models no LPDDR5, so the channel is a GDDR6 x16 channel at the same data rate, as Vortex's own gtx480 profile models GDDR5
sources.PLATFORM_CLOCK_RATE: 1020 MHz GPU clock of the Orin Nano Super's top power mode, so 12.8 GB/s is 12.5 bytes per core clock
sources.L2_SIZE: Per-core share of the GPU L2 (assumed 256 KB per SM; confirm against the research notes)
sources.L2_NUM_BANKS: 2 banks of 64 B per clock: more L2 bandwidth than one SM's share, so the L2 is not an artificial bottleneck
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: 0: host uploads bypass the L2, so every kernel starts with its data in DRAM, as in NVIDIA's batched benchmark whose data is far bigger than the L2
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY, PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: Calibrated with ci/profile_check.py to the reference latencies
sources.reference: l2_hit_cycles: about 200, as Vortex's calibrated Ampere A100 (200) and Turing T4 (188) profiles; dram_cycles: estimate for LPDDR5 at 1020 MHz, to be replaced by a measured Orin number if one is published
